title: Gray Leaf Spot of Maize - Nepal

Header: Gray Leaf Spot of Maize - Nepal
Cercospora zeae-maydis मकैकोपातमाला Შे ᭟वाँसे थे ᭏ले रोग

Prevention: It is extremely important to remove plant debris from previous diseased crops.
Rake up and burn the crop debris and to encourage your neighbours to do the same.
The disease can easily spread from debris in your neighbours fields.
The pathogen can survive on crop debris underground.
Ganesh-1, Manakamana-3 for high hills (1900 masl); and
Manakamana-1, Deuti, Manakamana-6, ZM401 for mid hills (1300 masl).
Proper tillage practices as early planting as possible.
The pathogen can survive for long periods in the soil.
Practice crop rotation for at least 3 years with non-host crops like millet, potato, vegetables, beans or pea.
Use recommended doses of chemical fertilizers (120:60:40
Monitoring: Monitor regularly for the appearance of gray leaf spot lesions on leaves just before or near initiation of tassel and ear shoot stage of plants grown at about 1400 masl.
Look for smaller chlorotic spots or lesions, first on lower leaves, which turn into long narrow rectangular lesions 2-3 weeks later.
Damage to the stalks may cause plants to fall over.
Take action as soon as disease symptom is seen.
Direct Control: To delay the disease, you can remove all the lower infected leaves at early stage of infection.
Bury them at least 50cm deep away from field or burn.
Practice this together with other adjoining farmers.
Restrictions: Use personal protection equipment while using fungicides.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Spray whole plant covering leaf, leaf sheath, stalk, ear shoot, as a protective measure, with carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/litre of water during first week of
July or at initiation of tassel in disease-prone areas where susceptible varieties are grown.
At least 35L of aqueous suspension of fungicide are required for 500 m2 area.
There is widespread resistance to this chemical and it should not be used in isolation.
A repeated spray at an interval of 15 days may be required depending on the disease severity.
